title: Mars Polar Lander (as it was meant to stand on Mars)
credit: Echoes of Exploration team (modelled in code from NASA reference drawings and photos)
note: Mars Polar Lander in its landed layout, 3.6 m across the solar wings with the deck 1.06 m above the ground: hexagonal deck over the gold insulated electronics box, two hydrazine tanks, three groups of four descent engines, three legs with footpads and touchdown sensors, two-piece solar wings on two sides plus two small auxiliary panels, the 2 m robotic arm with scoop and camera, the stereo camera on its lattice mast, the 1.2 m weather mast with its hanging sub-mast, the TEGA oven box, the lidar with the Mars Microphone, a steerable medium-gain dish and a UHF antenna. Simplified: instruments are approximate shapes and the solar-wing outline follows NASA artist's views. The real lander was lost while landing, so it never looked like this on Mars.
